steps.title: Keep only 2025 orders
steps.change: Both the monthly counts and the totals must use only 2025 orders.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, Total_Order_Amount
FROM Orders
WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2025'
ORDER BY OrderID;
steps.sql:
SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, Total_Order_Amount
FROM Orders
WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2025'
ORDER BY OrderID;

steps.title: Give each order its month label
steps.change: The first order in a month might have happened after the first. The label represents the calendar month.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, Total_Order_Amount,
       date(OrderDate, 'start of month') AS order_month
steps.sql:
SELECT OrderID, OrderDate, Total_Order_Amount,
       date(OrderDate, 'start of month') AS order_month
FROM Orders
WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2025'
ORDER BY OrderID;

steps.title: Group and count orders
steps.change: The year filter means a month number identifies one month in 2025. A month with no orders does not form a group.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT date(OrderDate, 'start of month') AS order_month,
       count(*) AS orders
-- …
GROUP BY strftime('%m', OrderDate)
ORDER BY strftime('%m', OrderDate) ASC;
steps.sql:
SELECT date(OrderDate, 'start of month') AS order_month,
       count(*) AS orders
FROM Orders
WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2025'
GROUP BY strftime('%m', OrderDate)
ORDER BY strftime('%m', OrderDate) ASC;

steps.title: Add the monthly total and ensure chronological order
steps.change: The count and sum describe the same order group. The explicit sort guarantees January precedes March.
steps.added_sql:
count(*) AS orders,
       sum(Total_Order_Amount) AS order_value
